input.body:
## Summary

```text
StageCapture: game canvas → Main flash layer
  └ PauseBackdrop (one retained bitmap)
      └ source history shared through Settings / Info
```

Replace the live CSS pause blur with the bitmap/history model from #26. Capture providers remain in browser/render services; simulation keeps its existing stage-frame rules.

## Evidence

- **Before:** Settings destroys the pause capture and CSS blurs the changing scene.
  **After:** native/mock proofs retain the same capture through Settings and Info, restore the opaque image exactly on reversal, delay gameplay resumption and release buffers/canvas on exit. Underlying artwork continues on its own clock.
- Formatting, TypeScript,438 tests /5653 assertions and production build pass. All20 focused native/mock game/menu/audio checks and the complete50-case mock/synthetic selection pass.
- Open/return captures inspected against stored original pause foreground13. The existing same-commit Dialog focus repair and pause phase/callback layout effects remain; only the active dialog owns focus/input.
- Native/mock effect replay and capture-provider ordering/state isolation are covered. No original media is committed.
- Capture covers the renderer and Main flash canvas. Arbitrary DOM overlays, two known mixed-RGB filter rounding differences, original event interleaving and synchronized original-stage pixel comparison remain limits. Full-game and Adobe parity remain unproven.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** menus

Changes pause capture ownership, Settings lifetime and backdrop rendering. Depends on #25/#26 and must land after their green CI.

--- title: use client description: Learn how to use the use client directive to render a component on the client. --- The `'use client'` directive declares an entry point for the components to be rendered on the **client side** and should be used when creating interactive user interfaces (UI) that require client-side JavaScript capabilities, such as state management, event handling, and access to browser APIs. This is a React feature. > **Good to know:** > > You do not need to add the `'use client'` directive to every file that contains Client Components. You only need to add it to the files whose components you want to render directly within Server Components. The `'use client'` directive defines the [server and client boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary), and the components exported from such a file serve as entry points to the client. ## Usage To declare an entry point for the Client Components, add the `'use client'` directive **at the top of the file**, before any imports. The directive applies to the entire module and cannot be placed inside a component or function: ```tsx filename="app/components/counter.tsx" highlight={1} switcher 'use client' import { useState } from 'react' export default function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0) return (
